To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the experience of the children, teachers, and students in this study was positive and that they all agreed that it should be replicated.
the experience of theatre and drama for children in early childhood education is an effective way to improve children's learning.

The experience of the Kubik project is an innovative educational experience that has the potential to be a resource for the training of early childhood teachers and for their work in the classroom, as well as a tool for reflection and debate on the educational role of art and drama in early childhood education and in the training of early years teachers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of a drama and art experience in early childhood education (0-6 years) through a qualitative methodology.
the analysis of the experience Kubik as a way to understand the pedagogical situation and to develop a new methodology for teacher training.
the analysis of an experience of art and dramatic play for the first year of primary education in the Basque Country.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the artistic experience of Kubik, as an example of an educational experience, is an innovative resource for the initial teacher education, as it allows to work with the variables of the situation of pedagogy: space-time, the teacher and educator, the child, the group and the world outside, in order to develop competences in children, and in teachers.
this experience is an innovative and creative way to work with children and to train future educators in the early stages of their professional development.

Kubik, as a pedagogical experience, is a model that can be applied to the training of teachers in the initial stage, as well as to the educational process of early childhood, and it is a resource and method that can be useful to develop and improve the competencies that are necessary for the professional exercise and personal growth of teachers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the research has allowed us to understand and interpret this educational reality, to analyze the pedagogical pillars on which it is based, and to assess whether it is suitable for providing resources to innovate and experiment in teacher education as well as in preschool education.

we have tried to show that the artistic and dramatic game can be an innovative resource and method to live and understand the variables of a pedagogical situation: space-time, the teacher and educator, the child, the group, and the outside world (Barrett, 1989).

we are trying to create a bridge between the arts and the school, between the culture of children and the culture of adults, through the creation and the study of a theatrical experience for children aged three to six years, called Kubik.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Kubik is a model of collaborative work where three audiences with a very different approach to education converge, but that share a common goal, namely to establish a connection between the performing arts, the infant school, and teacher training, that is, between the pedagogical and artistic, the child’s culture and that of adults.

the experience of the Kubik project is a good example to understand the relationship between the arts and education in early childhood, as well as the relationship between art and education in initial training of teachers.
we have been able to create a space for reflection and dialogue, where we can share experiences, ideas, doubts, and concerns, and where we can learn from each other.
